ideas.title: Mutation Nursery
ideas.core_loop: Collect wild plant/critter specimens and splice combinations in the nursery to produce mutations; failed splices consume the specimen, so every attempt carries real stakes. Rare mutations get sold or traded in a player market.
ideas.hook: Every mutation's lineage is server-tracked and displayable as a traceable lineage tree, so rarity is provable rather than claimed -- turning splicing outcomes into verifiable collectibles instead of another generic grow-and-sell loop.
ideas.economy_or_social_design: Player-to-player marketplace for rare lineages; failed splices act as an economy sink; displaying lineage trees on player plots is the social status hook.
ideas.ai_disclosure_note: AI would generate splice-outcome tables, mutation art prompts, and shop UI copy; the lineage-tracking backend and trade-security logic would need to be hand-built by a human developer.

ideas.title: The Lighthouse Watch
ideas.core_loop: Players work night shifts maintaining a lighthouse's systems (fuel, signal beacon, warding runes) while a fog-borne threat probes for whichever system is neglected; surviving to dawn banks resources toward permanent upgrades.
ideas.hook: The threat's behavior is systems-driven rather than scripted jump-scares -- it escalates specifically toward whatever you're failing to maintain, so mastery comes from triage under pressure and creates a genuine, learnable skill gap.
ideas.economy_or_social_design: Co-op crews of 2-4 share a lighthouse and split salvage; long-term upgrades are visible landmarks other players can see from outside, creating soft social status.
ideas.ai_disclosure_note: AI would generate fog-escalation event scripts, ambient audio cue lists, and night-event variety; a human would need to hand-tune the difficulty curve and system-interaction rules so it reads as fair rather than random.

ideas.title: Static Ave
ideas.core_loop: A no-objective neighborhood hangout where players rent and decorate storefronts and apartments, host small player-run events (open mic nights, garage sales), and socialize via spatial voice -- no combat, no grind.
ideas.hook: Rented storefronts function as player-run micro-businesses with an in-world postable schedule, so hangout activity is generated by the community itself instead of relying on scripted content drops to keep the space alive.
ideas.economy_or_social_design: Property rental is a soft-currency sink; player-hosted events drive session length and repeat visits; success is entirely dependent on community moderation tooling, not content volume.
ideas.ai_disclosure_note: AI would generate starter decor sets and neighborhood flavor text; genuine social trust, moderation tooling, and voice-chat safety systems must be human-designed and cannot be safely auto-generated.

ideas.title: Rent-a-Blorb
ideas.core_loop: Players hatch, feed, and rent out absurd meme-mashup creatures called Blorbs to other players' bases for short-term buffs; learnable in under 15 minutes.
ideas.hook: Instead of a one-off meme cash-grab, Blorbs generate ongoing rental income for their owners, giving the meme premise a light economy that can deepen post-launch (breeding, rare traits) rather than flattening after the initial spike.
ideas.economy_or_social_design: The rental marketplace is the core scarcity/trading loop; a breeding sink prevents rental-Blorb inflation; showing off rare Blorbs is the social hook.
ideas.ai_disclosure_note: AI would generate the initial wave of Blorb designs, names, and rental flavor text; a human needs to tune rental payout balance so the economy doesn't inflate within days.

ideas.title: Undertow Traders
ideas.core_loop: A deep-sea diving simulator where players harvest glowing resources on timed dives while oxygen depletes and a submerged threat reacts to noise and light; surfacing banks the haul, dying loses it.
ideas.hook: Merges the simulator collect-upgrade-unlock loop with horror_survival's escalating threat -- risk/reward is literal (how deep, how long) rather than abstract, and the threat's noise/light detection rewards players who learn its rules over those who react blindly.
ideas.economy_or_social_design: Harvested resources feed a player-run refinery/trading loop with crafting as a sink and dives as the faucet; high-risk dives produce bragging-rights loot that anchors social status and repeat play.
ideas.ai_disclosure_note: AI would generate resource/loot tables, dive-zone flavor text, and threat barks; the noise/light detection AI and dive-risk balancing need human tuning to avoid feeling either trivial or unfair.
